add.title: NJCM adviseert demissionair Minister voor Rechtsbescherming over plaatsing van transgender gedetineerden (Nederlands Juristen Comité voor de Mensenrechten)
add.summary: The Netherlands Jurists Committee for Human Rights (NJCM), criminal-law working group, announced (site date 22 Feb 2024) that it had advised the caretaker Minister for Legal Protection on the placement of transgender detainees: no law or regulation currently governs their placement, which NJCM calls worrying and undesirable. The note highlights the group's vulnerable position (international research documents human-rights violations including discrimination and sexual violence), the absence of official figures on the number of transgender detainees in the Netherlands, and the relevance of CPT standards, pointing to the full letter (PDF) to Minister Weerwind (21 Feb 2024).

add.title: Advies plaatsing transgender gedetineerden — brief aan de Minister voor Rechtsbescherming (NJCM Werkgroep Strafrecht, 21 februari 2024)
add.summary: NJCM letter to Minister Weerwind (Leiden, 21 Feb 2024) documenting Dutch placement practice for transgender detainees: there is no law, regulation or official policy governing their placement — the Penitentiary Principles Act only separates male and female detainees — and DJI (Prison Service) confirmed placement is based on the gender designation in the BRP (municipal records) together with case-by-case factors (gender-related physical features, the detainee's own preference, offence background, physical/mental health), while DIZ said it was (unpublished) drafting guidelines. Transgender detainees are frequently placed on an 'Extra Care Facility' (EZV) wing, generally to protect them from other detainees, where they sit alongside people with intellectual disabilities and sex offenders. The letter cites documented cases: a trans woman initially held on a regular male wing at arrival then moved to an EZV; a parole-board appeals ruling (21 Mar 2016, 15/4323/GB) on a trans woman first placed in a men's institution before transfer to the women's prison at Nieuwersluis, who reported intimidation, threats, assaults and molestation in the men's prison; and sentencing rulings by the Limburg court (17 Oct 2017, ECLI:NL:RBLIM:2017:10624, trans woman facing placement in a men's prison) and The Hague appeals court (29 Jun 2020, ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2020:1108, trans man in a women's prison) treating a wing not matching the detainee's gender as making imprisonment considerably heavier. NJCM asks the minister to create CPT-aligned rules placing transgender detainees by gender identity.
